nearbyCountiesFullText.description:
The officials at the Indiana Department of Environmental Management
have declared a Local Air Quality Advisory for Elkhart County, in
effect from 6 PM Saturday November 21st to 10 AM EST Sunday November
22nd.

A Local Air Quality Advisory for PM 2.5 has been issued. Fine
particulate levels are expected to be in the Unhealthy for Sensitive
Groups range. Active children and adults, and people with
respiratory disease, such as asthma should limit prolonged outdoor
exposure.

Due to observed and forecasted high concentration of PM2.5 readings
in the area, recommendations are for the public to reduce or avoid
exertion or heavy work outdoors and keep windows and doors closed as
much as possible.

For additional information, please visit the IDEM Smog page at:

http://www.in.gov/idem/airmonitoring/smogwatch/

discussion.text:
000
FXUS63 KIWX 220712
AFDIWX

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Northern Indiana
212 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Very mild once again before a cold front arrives to northwest
  Indiana late this afternoon.

- There is a 60% to 80% chance of showers starting early this
  afternoon. Rain amounts will be 0.10" or less. Rain exits by
  late evening. 

- Seasonably cold this week with highs near 40.

- Periods of rain and snow showers Wednesday evening through 
  Thursday (40-50% chance). 

&&

.DISCUSSION...
Issued at 211 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

High temperatures Saturday afternoon were a single degree shy of a 
1913 record at both Fort Wayne and South Bend amid an unseasonable 
500-mb ridge over the eastern CONUS. We'll cling to one more mild 
November day as the upper-air pattern remains amplified ahead of an 
approaching cold front. Filtered sunshine to begin the day followed 
by increasing clouds and rain arriving from east to east by the 
early afternoon. Somewhat breezy as well with southwest winds of 20-
25 mph. Rain amounts remain modest at 0.10" or less owing to the 
late-day timing and upper-level forcing displaced well to the 
northwest. Cool northwest flow sets in by the early evening hours 
propelling Sunday night lows toward freezing (clouds may keep 
northwest OH in the upper-30s). 

Very brief and inconsequential lake response from a secondary surge 
of cold air advection Monday night. Fetch and incoming high pressure 
limit the overall moister depth, but increasing concensus yields 
a narrow area (in both time and space) for 20% POPs. 

For late-week, the ECMWF has joined the GFS in what strikes me as an 
unusual evolution of dual upper-level lows emerging over the central 
and southern US. Concensus revels a deep trough in the lee of the 
Rockies, extending through far southern Texas. Encountering a 
subtropical ridge off the Florida coast this energy is shunted 
poleward along and east of the Mississippi River. The result is 
strong moisture transport and lackluster cold air given the 
competing air masses. POPs have increased locally to a 40-50% chance 
Wednesday evening through Tuesday with precipitation types generally 
following a diurnal curve (rain/snow overnight, changing to rain 
during the day).  The primary trough responsible for this system 
arrives to the west Coast tonight, improving model-guidance sampling 
in the near future.

In the wake of this feature, troughing favors the Midwest through 
the Thanksgiving weekend while zonal flow resumes for the start of 
December. 

&&

.AVIATION /06Z TAFS THROUGH 06Z MONDAY/...
Issued at 1222 AM EST Sun Nov 22 2026

A cold front approaches from the west today with a relatively thin 
line of moisture. Instability is rather minuscule and columnar 
moisture has some dry kinks in the armor, however, still think 
there's enough to lower flight conditions down into IFR for a few 
hours. Will use a TEMPO group for the IFR due to the kinks in the 
armor mentioned above. Otherwise, south winds veer southwesterly 
later this afternoon and could gust to 20 to 25 kts this evening. 
After an initial increase in low level lapse rates from diurnal 
warming today, another increase comes from an area of cold 
temperatures aloft meaning gusty winds could continue Sunday 
night into Monday.

&&

.IWX WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
IN...Air Quality Alert until 10 AM EST this morning for INZ005.
OH...None.
MI...None.
MARINE...Small Craft Advisory from 4 PM this afternoon to 4 AM EST 
     Tuesday for LMZ043-046.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Brown

spc.summary: Strong to locally severe storms are possible across parts of South Texas, mainly during the afternoon and early evening.
spc.text:
SPC AC 220545

   Day 1 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1145 PM CST Sat Nov 21 2026

   Valid 221200Z - 231200Z

   ...THERE IS A MARGINAL RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FOR PARTS OF
   SOUTH TX...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Strong to locally severe storms are possible across parts of South
   Texas, mainly during the afternoon and early evening.

   ...Synopsis...
   A mid/upper-level shortwave trough initially over the south-central
   Plains is forecast to move east-northeastward and gradually
   deamplify through the day. A cold front will move across parts of
   the Mississippi/Ohio Valleys and southern Plains. Farther east, a
   surface low is forecast to consolidate off of the Carolina coast and
   move northeastward, with the warm sector of this system expected to
   remain offshore.  

   ...South Texas...
   Rich low-level moisture and modest diurnal heating will result in
   moderate destabilization this afternoon, with MLCAPE increasing to
   the 1000-1500 J/kg range. Large-scale ascent associated with the
   departing shortwave trough will be displaced well to the north, but
   at least isolated storm development will be possible this afternoon
   along the front, and also potentially ahead of the front near the
   south TX coast. Moderate midlevel flow will provide sufficient
   deep-layer shear for storm organization, and isolated hail will be
   possible with the strongest storms. Locally strong gusts will also
   be possible, through very weak low-level flow and an anticipated
   lack of organized upscale growth will tend to limit severe-wind
   potential. 

   ...ArkLaTex into western TN/KY...
   Relatively strong heating will result in steepening low-level lapse
   rates along/ahead of the front later today from the ArkLaTex region
   into western TN/KY. However, modest low-level moisture and weak
   midlevel lapse rates will limit buoyancy, with MLCAPE forecast to
   only reach the 500-750 J/kg range by peak heating. Isolated diurnal 
   storm development will be possible along the front, with modestly
   favorable deep-layer shear potentially supporting transient storm
   organization. However, the weak thermodynamic environment is
   currently expected to limit severe potential, especially given the
   weakening trend of the ejecting shortwave trough across the region.

   ..Dean/Squitieri.. 11/22/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS01 PTSDY1 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 1 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1300Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 220654

   Day 2 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   1254 AM CST Sun Nov 22 2026

   Valid 231200Z - 241200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Severe storms are unlikely Monday.

   ...Synopsis...
   Mid-level troughing is forecast to intensify over the eastern Great
   Lakes and Northeastern US, dragging a strong cold front through the
   Gulf and off the Atlantic coast. To the west, a secondary, weaker
   trough will move from the Southwest into the Trans-Pecos. Between
   the two waves, transient mid-level ridging will reinforce strong
   surface high pressure in the post-frontal air mass over the central
   US.

   As the front continues offshore across the northern Gulf Coast,
   isentropic ascent may support isolated thunderstorms for a few hours
   across parts of southern LA/MS and AL. However this will be short
   lived through the first part of the day as available moisture will
   quickly be scoured southward with the advancing front. Similar
   conditions may briefly develop across far south TX. Given the weak
   buoyancy and shear, severe storms are unlikely.

   Isolated thunderstorms are also possible with the secondary trough
   across NM into far west TX. Cool mid-level temperatures, but very
   modest moisture may support occasional lightning through the
   overnight hours. Severe storms are not expected.

   ..Lyons.. 11/22/2026

   CLICK TO GET WUUS02 PTSDY2 PRODUCT

   NOTE: THE NEXT DAY 2 OUTLOOK IS SCHEDULED BY 1730Z

spc.text:
SPC AC 220830

   Day 3 Convective Outlook  
   NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
   0230 AM CST Sun Nov 22 2026

   Valid 241200Z - 251200Z

   ...NO SEVERE THUNDERSTORM AREAS FORECAST...

   ...SUMMARY...
   Isolated thunderstorms are possible over parts of the Gulf Coast and
   West Coast Tuesday. Severe storms are not expected.

   ...Synopsis...
   An upper trough over the southern Plains is forecast to intensify as
   it moves southeastward across TX toward the Gulf Coast Tuesday and
   Tuesday night. In the wake of a prior cold front, low-level moisture
   will remain confined near the Gulf Coast across TX and into the
   Southeast. Scattered thunderstorms are expected along typical sea
   breeze corridors across the FL Peninsula during the day. Strong
   mid-level ascent from the approaching trough and a weak surface
   low/inverted surface trough over the Gulf may also support an
   elevated band of showers and isolated thunderstorms over parts of
   MS/AL Tuesday night into early Wednesday.

   To the west, an approaching Pacific trough and cold front are
   forecast to move inland across northern CA into early Wednesday.
   Onshore flow may support weak buoyancy along the coast, with a
   narrow band of shallow convection potentially supporting occasional
   lightning flashes into Wednesday morning. Given the weak overall
   buoyancy and poor overlap with strong vertical shear, severe storms
   are not expected.

   ..Lyons.. 11/22/2026

consensus.about: NWS next to four computer models (Open-Meteo, CC BY 4.0). blend = the middle value of NWS and the models; adjusted = blend corrected by our own average past error at the La Porte airport once 14+ days are graded (capped at 3 degrees). Rain chances are NWS's. suggested = what the Daily Scoop's forecasts use (tomorrow and the day after).

bias.note: Average of (forecast minus airport reading) over the last 30 graded days; positive means we ran warm. Used to nudge the model blend once 14+ days are graded.
